items.title: Additive per-step errors in a Lipschitzian one-step scheme accumulate geometrically: $\eta((1+Lh)^n-1)/(Lh)$

references.title: E. Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration (TU Munchen 2010), Lecture 3 'Backward error analysis', Section 3: accumulation of per-step perturbations with a Lipschitz constant, the summation argument for long-time energy estimates, printed pages 6-7
A. Quillen, PHY411 Lecture notes Part 7 'Integrators' (University of Rochester), Section 1.1: accumulation of per-step errors versus local truncation errors for one-step methods, printed pages 2-5

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space ([[def-metric-space]]), let $V:X\to X$ map $X$ into itself, and let $L\ge0$ and $h>0$. Assume

$$d\bigl(V(x),V(y)\bigr)\le(1+Lh)\,d(x,y)\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in X,$$

which is a Lipschitz hypothesis on $V$ with constant $1+Lh$ ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]]). Fix $z_0\in X$, put $z_{j+1}:=V(z_j)$ for $j\in\mathbb N$, and let $x_0:=z_0$ together with points $x_{j+1}\in X$ satisfying

$$d\bigl(x_{j+1},V(x_j)\bigr)\le\eta\qquad(j\in\mathbb N)$$

for a number $\eta\ge0$ ("computational error per step"). Then for every $n\in\mathbb N$:

1. if $L>0$, $\displaystyle d(x_n,z_n)\le\eta\,\frac{(1+Lh)^n-1}{Lh}$, and if $L=0$, $d(x_n,z_n)\le n\eta$;
2. if moreover $F:X\to\mathbb R$ satisfies the Lipschitz bound $|F(x)-F(y)|\le\Lambda\,d(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$ and some $\Lambda<\infty$, then
 $$|F(x_n)-F(z_n)|\le\Lambda\eta\,\frac{(1+Lh)^n-1}{Lh}\quad(L>0),\qquad |F(x_n)-F(z_n)|\le\Lambda n\eta\quad(L=0);$$
3. if $nh\le T$ for some $T>0$ and $L>0$, then $(1+Lh)^n\le e^{LT}$ and therefore
 $$d(x_n,z_n)\le\eta\,\frac{e^{LT}-1}{Lh}\le \eta\,e^{LT}\frac{T}{h}.$$

items.title: Complex phase domains, holomorphic maps on $\mathbb C^m$, and the complexified canonical form and bracket

references.title: J. Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 1, Section 1.1 (holomorphic functions in several variables) and Section 1.2 (polydiscs and power series), printed pages 13-27

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
**Holomorphic maps.** Let $m,p\ge1$ and let $D\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open, identified with an open subset of $\mathbb R^{2m}$ through $\mathbb C^m\cong\mathbb R^{2m}$. A map $F:D\to\mathbb C^p$ is **complex differentiable at** $a\in D$ when there is a map $L:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^p$ that is $\mathbb C$-linear — $L(u+v)=L(u)+L(v)$ and $L(\lambda u)=\lambda L(u)$ for $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-linear-map]], [[def-euclidean-linear-map]], [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]) — with

$$F(a+v)=F(a)+L(v)+r(v),\qquad \frac{\lVert r(v)\rVert}{\lVert v\rVert}\longrightarrow0\ \ (v\to0),$$

the norm being the Euclidean norm of $\mathbb R^{2m}$ and $\mathbb R^{2p}$ ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]). Such an $L$ is unique by the argument of [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]], applied componentwise; it is denoted $DF(a)$. The map $F$ is **holomorphic on** $D$ when it is complex differentiable at every point of $D$; for $m=p=1$ this is the notion of [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]. For holomorphic $F$ and $k\le m$ put $\partial_{z_k}F(a):=DF(a)(e_k)$, the $k$-th coordinate derivative; for $p=1$ this is the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] in the complex coordinate direction.

**Real analytic functions.** Let $N\ge1$ and let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ be open. A function $\varphi:V\to\mathbb R$ is **real analytic at** $x\in V$ when there are an open set $W\subseteq\mathbb C^N$ with $x\in W$ and a holomorphic $F:W\to\mathbb C$ with $F(\xi)=\varphi(\xi)$ for every $\xi\in W\cap V$; $\varphi$ is **real analytic on** $V$ when it is real analytic at every point of $V$. Thus real analyticity is defined here exactly as *admitting a local holomorphic extension*.

**Polydiscs.** For $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and a polyradius $\rho=(\rho_1,\dots,\rho_m)$ with $0<\rho_k\le\infty$ put

$$\Delta_\rho(a):=\{\,z\in\mathbb C^m:\ |z_k-a_k|<\rho_k\ \text{for all }k\,\},\qquad \Gamma_\rho(a):=\{\,z:\ |z_k-a_k|=\rho_k\ \text{for all }k\,\},$$

the open **polydisc** and its **distinguished boundary**; a polydisc is open and convex ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-metric-topology]]).

**Complex phase domains.** Let $d\ge1$. A **complex phase domain** is a nonempty open $D\subseteq\mathbb C^{2d}$ whose points are written $Z=(z,w)$ with $z=(z^1,\dots,z^d)$, $w=(w_1,\dots,w_d)\in\mathbb C^d$. On it define the **complexified canonical two-form** and the **complexified Poisson bracket** of holomorphic functions $f,g:D\to\mathbb C$ by

$$\omega_{\mathbb C}:=\sum_{i=1}^d dz^i\wedge dw_i,\qquad \{f,g\}:=\sum_{i=1}^d\bigl(\partial_{z^i}f\,\partial_{w_i}g-\partial_{w_i}f\,\partial_{z^i}g\bigr),$$

and for a holomorphic $f:D\to\mathbb C$ its **complex Hamiltonian field** $X_f:=J\nabla f$, where $J=\begin{pmatrix}0_d&I_d\\-I_d&0_d\end{pmatrix}$ is the standard symplectic matrix of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]] and $\nabla f=(\partial_{z^1}f,\dots,\partial_{z^d}f,\partial_{w_1}f,\dots,\partial_{w_d}f)$ is the gradient column of coordinate derivatives. The real subspace $\mathbb R^{2d}\subseteq\mathbb C^{2d}$ and the restriction of $\omega_{\mathbb C}$, $J$ and $\{\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\}$ to real-valued functions reproduce the real objects of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]].

**Distance domains.** For $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$ and $r>0$ put

$$D(r):=\{\,\zeta\in\mathbb C^{2d}:\ \operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\overline U)<r\,\},\qquad \operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\overline U):=\inf\{\lVert\zeta-x\rVert:x\in\overline U\},$$

where $\overline U$ is the closure of $U$ in $\mathbb R^{2d}$ and the norm is the Euclidean norm of $\mathbb C^{2d}\cong\mathbb R^{4d}$. Each $D(r)$ is open, contains $U$, and $D(r)\subseteq D(r')$ for $r\le r'$; if $U$ is star-shaped with respect to $0$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]), then every $D(r)$ is star-shaped with respect to $0$ as well.

items.title: The splitting Hamiltonian $H=A+B$, the drift and kick maps, and the velocity-Verlet map

references.title: E. Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration (TU Munchen 2010), Lecture 2 'Symplectic integrators', Sections 1 and 5: the Stormer-Verlet scheme and its interpretation as the Strang splitting of the kinetic and potential flows, printed pages 1-3 and 12-13
A. Quillen, PHY411 Lecture notes Part 7 'Integrators' (University of Rochester), Sections 2.3 and 2.5: drift and kick evolution operators and the Stormer-Verlet method, printed pages 18-20 and 23-24

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$ be a phase domain with coordinates $z=(q,p)$, $q=(q^1,\dots,q^d)$ and $p=(p_1,\dots,p_d)$, standard two-form $\omega_U=\sum_i dq^i\wedge dp_i$ and standard symplectic matrix $J$ ([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]).

Fix a matrix $M\in M_d(\mathbb R)$ that is **symmetric and positive definite**, meaning $M^{\mathsf T}=M$ ([[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]) and $v^{\mathsf T}Mv>0$ for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb R^d$; here $v^{\mathsf T}Mv$ is the matrix product of [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]. Fix an open $\Pi\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ with $U\subseteq\Pi\times\mathbb R^d$ and a function $U_{\mathrm{pot}}:\Pi\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), whose gradient $\nabla U_{\mathrm{pot}}$ and Hessian matrix $H_{U_{\mathrm{pot}}}$ are those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and [[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]; write $\nabla U_{\mathrm{pot}}(q)$ as a column vector and abbreviate $U_{\mathrm{pot}}(q)$ by $V(q)$ on $U$.

On $U$ define the **kinetic part** and **potential part**

$$A(q,p):=\tfrac12\,p^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}p,\qquad B(q,p):=V(q),\qquad H:=A+B,$$

and the **drift** and **kick** maps $D_h,K_h:U\to\mathbb R^{2d}$,

$$D_h(q,p):=(q+h\,M^{-1}p,\;p),\qquad K_h(q,p):=(q,\;p-h\,\nabla V(q)).$$

Both are defined wherever their displayed values lie in $U$; in particular $D_h$ is defined on $U$ whenever $(q+hM^{-1}p,p)\in U$, and $K_h$ on $U$ whenever $(q,p-h\nabla V(q))\in U$. The **velocity-Verlet map** of the splitting $H=A+B$ at step $h\in\mathbb R$ is the composite

$$V_h:=K_{h/2}\circ D_h\circ K_{h/2},$$

defined on the set of $(q,p)\in U$ for which the composition exists and its value lies in $U$.

items.title: Iterated Cauchy formula, power-series expansion and Cauchy estimates for functions continuous and separately holomorphic on a polydisc

references.title: J. Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 1, Theorem 1.2.1 and the Cauchy estimates following Proposition 1.2.2, printed pages 18-23

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, let $a\in\mathbb C^m$, let $\rho$ be a polyradius with $0<\rho_k<\infty$, and let $f:\Delta_\rho(a)\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and holomorphic in each variable separately, that is, for every $k$ and every choice of the other coordinates the slice $\zeta\mapsto f(\dots,\zeta,\dots)$ is holomorphic on its open disc ([[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]], [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]). For a polyradius $r$ with $r_k<\rho_k$ put $M(r):=\sup_{\Gamma_r(a)}|f|$, a finite number.

Then:

1. **Iterated Cauchy formula.** For every $z\in\Delta_r(a)$,
 $$f(z)=\frac{1}{(2\pi i)^m}\oint_{|\zeta_1-a_1|=r_1}\cdots\oint_{|\zeta_m-a_m|=r_m}\frac{f(\zeta)}{\prod_{k}(\zeta_k-z_k)}\,d\zeta_1\cdots d\zeta_m,$$
 and the iterated integrals in any order of the variables agree.
2. **Power-series expansion.** For every polyradius $r'$ with $r_k<r'_k<\rho_k$, and every $z\in\Delta_r(a)$,
 $$f(z)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^m}c_\alpha\,(z-a)^\alpha,\qquad c_\alpha=\frac{1}{(2\pi i)^m}\oint_{\Gamma_{r'}(a)}\frac{f(\zeta)\,d\zeta}{(\zeta-a)^{\alpha+\mathbf 1}},$$
 where the coefficients $c_\alpha$ do not depend on $r'$, the series converges absolutely and uniformly on every compact subset of $\Delta_\rho(a)$, and $|c_\alpha|\le M(r')\prod_k (r'_k)^{-\alpha_k}$.
3. **Holomorphy, derivatives and estimates.** The function $f$ is holomorphic on $\Delta_\rho(a)$ in the sense of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]]. Its coordinate derivatives $\partial_{z_k}f$ exist everywhere on $\Delta_\rho(a)$, are continuous and holomorphic in each variable separately there, and satisfy, for $0<s_k<\rho_k$,
 $$|\partial_{z_k}f(a)|\le\frac{M(s)}{s_k}.$$

items.title: The velocity-Verlet step matches the exact flow through order two: local truncation error $O(h^3)$ on a convex tube

references.title: E. Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration (TU Munchen 2010), Lecture 2 'Symplectic integrators', Theorem 2 and Section 5: the Stormer-Verlet method is of order 2 and is the Strang splitting of the kinetic and potential flows, printed pages 1-3 and 12-13

A. Quillen, PHY411 Lecture notes Part 7 'Integrators' (University of Rochester), Sections 1.1-1.2 and 2.5: Taylor comparison of one-step methods with the exact flow and the second-order Stormer-Verlet update, printed pages 2-7 and 23-24

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $U$, $M$, $V$, $A$, $B$, $H=A+B$, $D_h$, $K_h$ and $V_h$ be as in [[def-cm-splitting-hamiltonian-and-verlet-map]]. Let $W\subseteq U$ be open, bounded and convex, let $K\subseteq W$ be nonempty compact, and let $r>0$ satisfy $K+\overline B_r(0)\subseteq W$ ([[def-metric-ball]]). Put

$$X_H(q,p):=(M^{-1}p,\,-\nabla V(q)),\qquad M_0:=\sup_W\lVert X_H\rVert,\quad L_1:=\sup_W\lVert DX_H\rVert,\quad L_2:=\sup_W\lVert D^2X_H\rVert,$$

the derivatives being the total derivatives with operator norms ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]); assume all three numbers are finite (for example, this holds when $\overline W\subseteq U$). Let $\Phi_t$ be the local flow of $X_H$ ([[def-cm-local-flow-of-an-autonomous-system]]).

Then there exist $h_0>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on $d$, $r$, $\lVert M^{-1}\rVert$, $\sup_K\lVert p\rVert$, $M_0$, $L_1$ and $L_2$, such that for every $(q,p)\in K$ and every $0<|h|\le h_0$:

1. $\Phi_h(q,p)$ is defined and lies in $W$, and
 $$\Bigl\lVert\Phi_h(q,p)-(q,p)-hX_H(q,p)-\tfrac{h^2}{2}DX_H(q,p)X_H(q,p)\Bigr\rVert\le C|h|^3.$$
2. $V_h(q,p)$ is defined and lies in $W$, and its two block components satisfy
 $$V_h(q,p)=\Bigl(q+hM^{-1}p-\tfrac{h^2}{2}M^{-1}\nabla V(q)+\rho_1,\;\; p-h\nabla V(q)-\tfrac{h^2}{2}H_V(q)M^{-1}p+\rho_2\Bigr)$$
 with $\lVert\rho_1\rVert,\lVert\rho_2\rVert\le C|h|^3$; equivalently $V_h$ and $\Phi_h$ have the same expansion through order two,
 $$X_H(q,p)=\bigl(M^{-1}p,\,-\nabla V(q)\bigr),\qquad DX_H(q,p)X_H(q,p)=\bigl(-M^{-1}\nabla V(q),\,-H_V(q)M^{-1}p\bigr).$$
3. Consequently $\lVert V_h(q,p)-\Phi_h(q,p)\rVert\le C|h|^3$ for every $(q,p)\in K$ and $0<|h|\le h_0$.

items.title: Calculus of holomorphic maps: chain rule, Wirtinger derivatives, coefficient extraction in one variable, and locally uniform limits

references.title: J. Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 1, Sections 1.1-1.3 (holomorphic maps, power series, derivatives), printed pages 13-31

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $m,l,p\ge1$ and let $D\subseteq\mathbb C^m$, $D'\subseteq\mathbb C^l$ be open, with holomorphy in the sense of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]].

1. **Chain rule.** If $g:D'\to D$ and $F:D\to\mathbb C^p$ are holomorphic, then $F\circ g:D'\to\mathbb C^p$ is holomorphic and
 $$D(F\circ g)(z)=DF\bigl(g(z)\bigr)\circ Dg(z)\qquad(z\in D').$$
2. **Wirtinger derivatives and the bracket matrix.** If $f:D\to\mathbb C$ is holomorphic, then $f$ is totally differentiable as a map of $\mathbb R^{2m}$ and, writing $x_k,y_k$ for the real and imaginary parts of $z_k$,
 $$\partial_{\bar z_k}f:=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_{x_k}f+i\,\partial_{y_k}f\bigr)=0,\qquad \partial_{z_k}f:=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_{x_k}f-i\,\partial_{y_k}f\bigr)=Df(e_k).$$
 Consequently, for holomorphic $f,g$ on a complex phase domain $D\subseteq\mathbb C^{2d}$, with $\nabla f=(\partial_{z^1}f,\dots,\partial_{w_d}f)$ and $J$ the standard matrix,
 $$\{f,g\}=(\nabla f)^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g.$$
3. **Coefficient extraction in a complex step variable.** Let $0<\sigma\le\infty$ and let $D\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open, and let $F:\{|h|<\sigma\}\times D\to\mathbb C^p$ be holomorphic. Then for every $j\in\mathbb N$ the coefficient map
 $$c_j(z):=\partial_h^jF(0,z)/j!$$
 is holomorphic on $D$, and for every $0<s<\sigma$, $c_j(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|h|=s}\frac{F(h,z)}{h^{j+1}}\,dh$.
4. **Locally uniform limits.** If $F_n:D\to\mathbb C^p$ are holomorphic and $F_n\to F$ locally uniformly on $D$ in the sense of [[rem-locally-uniform-convergence-dictionary]] and [[def-uniform-convergence-of-complex-valued-functions]], then $F$ is holomorphic on $D$.

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $U$, $M$, $V$, $A$, $B$, $H=A+B$, $D_h$, $K_h$ and $V_h$ be as in [[def-cm-splitting-hamiltonian-and-verlet-map]], with $\omega_U$ the standard two-form and $J=\begin{pmatrix}0_d&I_d\\-I_d&0_d\end{pmatrix}$ the standard symplectic matrix ([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]). Then, on the sets where the maps are defined:

1. $D_h$ is $C^\infty$ with constant derivative
 $$DD_h(q,p)=\begin{pmatrix}I_d&hM^{-1}\\0_d&I_d\end{pmatrix},$$
 and, when the whole segment $(q+tM^{-1}p,p)$ for $t$ between $0$ and $h$ lies in $U$, $D_h(q,p)$ is the time-$h$ value of the local flow ([[def-cm-local-flow-of-an-autonomous-system]]) of the Hamiltonian field $X_A(q,p)=(M^{-1}p,0)$ of the kinetic part; moreover
 $$DD_h(q,p)^{\mathsf T}J\,DD_h(q,p)=J.$$
2. $K_h$ is $C^2$ with derivative
 $$DK_h(q,p)=\begin{pmatrix}I_d&0_d\\-h\,H_V(q)&I_d\end{pmatrix},$$
 where $H_V$ is the Hessian matrix of $V$, and, when the whole segment $(q,p-t\nabla V(q))$ for $t$ between $0$ and $h$ lies in $U$, $K_h(q,p)$ is the time-$h$ value of the local flow of the Hamiltonian field $X_B(q,p)=(0,-\nabla V(q))$ of the potential part; moreover
 $$DK_h(q,p)^{\mathsf T}J\,DK_h(q,p)=J.$$
3. The admissible composition domain of $V_h$ is open, $V_h$ is $C^2$ there, and its derivative satisfies
 $$DV_h(q,p)^{\mathsf T}J\,DV_h(q,p)=J,$$
 so that $V_h^*\omega_U=\omega_U$: the velocity-Verlet map preserves the standard two-form and is a local $C^2$ canonical transformation in the finite-regularity sense of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]. This matrix/form conclusion holds on the full algebraic composition domain; the separate flow interpretations in clauses 1-2 require the stated intermediate-segment containment.

items.title: Analytic splitting data with uniform holomorphic neighbourhood, and the exact symmetric splitting map $\Psi_h$

references.title: E. Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration (TU Munchen 2010), Lecture 3 'Backward error analysis', Sections 1-3: the modified differential equation of a splitting method, the modified Hamiltonian for symplectic methods and the star-shaped global existence remark, printed pages 1-7
J. Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 1, Sections 1.1-1.2: holomorphic maps, polydiscs and separate holomorphy on complex domains, printed pages 13-27

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. **Analytic splitting data** consists of the following objects.

1. A nonempty open bounded set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$, star-shaped with respect to $0$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]), together with a number $\rho>0$ and the **uniform holomorphic neighbourhood** $U_\rho:=D(\rho)=\{\zeta\in\mathbb C^{2d}:\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\overline U)<\rho\}$ of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]].
2. Functions $A,B:U\to\mathbb R$ (written additively as the **splitting** $H:=A+B$) that are real analytic on $U$ and admit **holomorphic extensions** $\tilde A,\tilde B:U_\rho\to\mathbb C$ with $\tilde A|_U=A$ and $\tilde B|_U=B$, where holomorphy is the $\mathbb C$-linear total-derivative notion of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]].
3. A constant $M\ge1$ with $\lVert X_{\tilde A}\rVert\le M$ and $\lVert X_{\tilde B}\rVert\le M$ pointwise on $U_\rho$, where $X_F=J\nabla F$ is the complex Hamiltonian field of a holomorphic $F$ and the norm is the Euclidean norm of $\mathbb C^{2d}\cong\mathbb R^{4d}$ ([[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]], [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]).
4. A nonempty compact $K\subseteq U$, star-shaped with respect to $0$; then $\delta:=\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathbb R^{2d}\setminus U)>0$ because $K$ is compact, $\mathbb R^{2d}\setminus U$ is closed and the two sets are disjoint ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]], [[def-metric-topology]], [[lem-relative-compact-closed-sets-have-a-positive-distance-gap]]).

For $t\in\mathbb C$ and $F\in\{\tilde A,\tilde B\}$ denote by $\varphi_F^t$ the local flow of the holomorphic field $X_F$, meaning the (unique) maximal solution family of $\frac{d}{d\tau}Y(\tau)=X_F(Y(\tau))$, $Y(0)=Z$ in complex time $\tau$; its existence, uniqueness and differentiability are supplied by [[lem-cm-complex-analytic-flow-existence-and-holomorphy]] on this page, and the objects below are used only on the domains where the three flows are defined.

The **exact splitting map** at step $h\in\mathbb C$ is

$$\Psi_h:=\varphi_{\tilde A}^{h/2}\circ\varphi_{\tilde B}^{h}\circ\varphi_{\tilde A}^{h/2},$$

defined wherever the composition exists; for $m\in\mathbb N$ its $m$-th iterate is $\Psi_h^m:=\Psi_h\circ\cdots\circ\Psi_h$ ($m$ factors, $\Psi_h^0=\mathrm{id}$).

items.title: Finite-time global error of the velocity-Verlet method: $\lVert z_n-\Phi_{nh}(z_0)\rVert\le C(e^{LT}-1)h^2/L$

references.title: E. Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration (TU Munchen 2010), Lecture 2 'Symplectic integrators', Sections 1-2 and 4: order of a one-step method and composition of consistent methods, printed pages 1-9
A. Quillen, PHY411 Lecture notes Part 7 'Integrators' (University of Rochester), Sections 1.1-1.2: local versus global error accumulation for one-step methods, printed pages 2-7

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Use the data, finite field and derivative bounds, and constants $h_1,C_1$ of [[lem-cm-verlet-local-truncation-error-is-cubic]] on an open bounded convex tube $W$, with compact $K_1$ and positive tube margin. Let $T>0$, $0<|h|\le h_1$, and $n\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $n|h|\le T$. Suppose $z_j=V_h^j(z_0)$ and $y_j=\Phi_{jh}(z_0)$ both lie in $K_1$ for $0\le j\le n$. With $L=L_1=\sup_W\|DX_H\|$, the following holds:

$$\|z_n-y_n\|\le C_1h^2\frac{e^{LT}-1}{L}\quad(L>0),\qquad \|z_n-y_n\|\le C_1Th^2\quad(L=0).$$

The constants are independent of $n,h,T$, with the displayed data fixed.

items.title: The flow of a bounded holomorphic field on a polydisc: existence in complex time, displacement bound, holomorphy, and the composition law

references.title: J. Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 1, Sections 1.1-1.3: holomorphic functions, power series and continuous dependence on data, printed pages 13-31

E. Hairer, Geometric Numerical Integration (TU Munchen 2010), Lecture 3 'Backward error analysis', Section 1: Taylor expansion of the flow of a modified vector field and the formal expansion of a one-step method, printed pages 1-3

items.design_state: Fully authored draft; outside artifact completion cycle 1; independent native review remains pending
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb C^n$ be holomorphic in the sense of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]] with $\lVert F\rVert\le M$ everywhere on $D$ for some $M>0$, let $Z_0\in D$ and let $s>0$ satisfy $\Delta_s(Z_0)\subseteq D$ ([[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]]). Put

$$t_0:=\frac{s}{8nM},\qquad D_{t_0}:=\{t\in\mathbb C:\ |t|\le t_0\}.$$

Then there is a map $\Phi:D_{t_0}\times B(Z_0,s/4)\to D$ such that:

1. **Solution.** For every $Z\in B(Z_0,s/4)$ the curve $t\mapsto\Phi(t,Z)$ is the unique solution of $\frac{d}{d\tau}Y(\tau)=F(Y(\tau))$, $Y(0)=Z$, on $D_{t_0}$ among all solutions with values in the ball $B(Z,s/2)$; it satisfies $\lVert\Phi(t,Z)-Z\rVert\le M|t|$ and $\|\Phi(t,Z)-Z\|\le s/(8n)$.
2. **Holomorphy.** $\Phi$ is holomorphic on the open set $\{|t|<t_0\}\times B(Z_0,s/4)$ in the sense of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]], and $\Phi(0,Z)=Z$.
3. **Composition and inverse.** The local solutions glue uniquely on overlapping initial-data balls. For the resulting local flow, whenever both sides are defined on the same connected continuation of the solution, $\Phi(s_2,\Phi(s_1,Z))=\Phi(s_1+s_2,Z)$. In particular, for sufficiently small $s_1$ for which the forward and backward local solutions exist, $\Phi(-s_1,\Phi(s_1,Z))=Z$. No assertion that every translated point remains in the displayed initial-data ball is made.

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $(U,U_\rho,\tilde A,\tilde B,M,K,\delta,\Psi_h)$ be analytic splitting data as in [[def-cm-analytic-splitting-data-and-exact-splitting-map]], with complexified form and bracket as in [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]]. For $r>0$ put $D(r):=\{\zeta\in\mathbb C^{2d}:\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\overline U)<r\}$.

There is a constant $C_0=C_0(d)\ge1$ such that for every integer $N\ge2$, with

$$b:=\frac{\rho}{8N},\qquad r_N:=\frac{\rho}{C_0MN},\qquad q:=\frac{C_dM|h|}{b},$$

the following holds for every complex $h$ with $0<|h|\le r_N$. Write $D_k:=D(\rho/2-2bk)$ for $0\le k\le N$; then $D_0=D(\rho/2)$, $D_N=D(\rho/4)\supseteq K$, and $D_N\subseteq D_k\subseteq D_0$ for $k\le N$. Define the **difference operator**

$$\Delta_hf:=f\circ\Psi_h-f$$

for functions $f$ holomorphic on $D_{k-1}$, where the composition is read on $D_k$. Then:

1. **Domain control.** For every $k=1,\dots,N$ the map $\Psi_h$ is holomorphic on $D_k$, maps $D_k$ into $D_{k-1}$, and satisfies $\lVert\Psi_h(Z)-Z\rVert\le2M|h|\le b$ for all $Z\in D_k$.
2. **Single-step bound.** If $f$ is holomorphic on $D_{k-1}$ with $|f|\le F$ there, then $\Delta_hf$ is holomorphic on $D_k$ and
 $$\lvert\Delta_hf(Z)\rvert\le\frac{C_dM|h|}{b}\,F\qquad(Z\in D_k),$$
 with $C_d:=4d^2$.
3. **Iterates.** Taking $C_0:=\max\{16,\,128d^2\}$ one has $q\le1/4$ for $|h|\le r_N$, and for every $f$ holomorphic on $D_0$ and every $1\le k\le N$, the iterate $\Delta_h^kf$ is holomorphic on $D_k$ and
 $$\lvert\Delta_h^kf(Z)\rvert\le q^k\,|f|_{D_0}\qquad(Z\in D_k).$$

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $(U,U_\rho,\tilde A,\tilde B,M,K,\delta,\Psi_h)$ be analytic splitting data ([[def-cm-analytic-splitting-data-and-exact-splitting-map]]), let $C_0=C_0(d)$ be the constant of [[lem-cm-difference-operator-and-domain-loss-bound]], and fix the notation $D(r)$, $b=\rho/(8N)$, $r_N=\rho/(C_0MN)$ and $D_k=D(\rho/2-2bk)$ of that lemma. Throughout, $N\ge2$ is an integer, $|h|\le r_N$, and all functions are read on the domain $D_N$ unless stated otherwise.

**Binomial coefficients.** For $s\in\mathbb C$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ define

$$\binom{s}{k}:=\frac{\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}(s-i)}{k!},$$

the empty product being $1$, and $k!$ the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]] embedded in $\mathbb C$; thus $\binom{s}{0}=1$, $\binom{s}{k}$ is a polynomial in $s$ of degree $k$ with rational coefficients, $\binom{m}{k}$ agrees with the elementary count for integers $m$, and

$$\left.\frac{d}{ds}\binom{s}{k}\right|_{s=0}=\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}\quad(k\ge1),\qquad \left.\frac{d}{ds}\binom{s}{0}\right|_{s=0}=0.$$

**Difference operator and pullbacks.** For $f$ holomorphic on $D_0$ put $\Delta_hf:=f\circ\Psi_h-f$, a holomorphic function on $D_1$ by [[lem-cm-difference-operator-and-domain-loss-bound]]; for $k\ge0$ let $\Delta_h^kf$ be the $k$-fold iterate, holomorphic on $D_k$, and let $\Psi_h^m$ be the $m$-fold iterate of $\Psi_h$ (so $\Psi_h^0=\mathrm{id}$).

**Truncated binomial family.** For $s\in\mathbb C$, $f$ holomorphic on $D_0$ and $Z\in D_N$ define

$$T_h^{s,N}f:=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\binom{s}{k}\,\Delta_h^kf,$$

a finite sum of functions each holomorphic on $D_k\supseteq D_N$: it is a holomorphic function on $D_N$, and for fixed $h$ and $f$ the map $s\mapsto T_h^{s,N}f$ is a polynomial of degree at most $N$ with values in the holomorphic functions on $D_N$.

**Truncated logarithm and coefficient fields.** The **truncated logarithm** is

$$L_N(h)f:=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}\,\Delta_h^kf=T_h^{s,N}f\Big|_{s=0}\text{ differentiated in }s,$$

that is, $L_N(h)f=\frac{d}{ds}\bigl(T_h^{s,N}f\bigr)\big|_{s=0}$; it is holomorphic on $D_N$. For $1\le j\le N$ and each coordinate function $z_i$ ($i=1,\dots,2d$), the function $h\mapsto(L_N(h)z_i)(Z)$ is holomorphic on $\{|h|\le r_N\}$ and vanishes at $h=0$ (each $\Delta_h^kz_i$ is $O(h^k)$), so the quotient $(L_N(h)z_i)(Z)/h$ has a removable singularity at $h=0$ and a well-defined Taylor coefficient of $h^{j-1}$; define the **$j$-th coefficient field** $X_j:D_N\to\mathbb C^{2d}$ by

$$(X_j)_i(Z):=\bigl[h^{j-1}\bigr]\frac{(L_N(h)z_i)(Z)}{h}\qquad(Z\in D_N,\ i=1,\dots,2d),$$

the coefficient being extracted by Cauchy's formula in the one variable $h$ ([[lem-cm-holomorphic-map-calculus]] clause 3). Finally the **truncation of the modified field** at order $N$ is

$$X^{[N]}(h):=\sum_{j=1}^{N}h^{j-1}X_j,$$

a holomorphic map $D_N\to\mathbb C^{2d}$ for every $|h|\le r_N$.

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $(U,U_\rho,\tilde A,\tilde B,M,K,\delta,\Psi_h)$ be analytic splitting data, and use all notation of [[def-cm-modified-log-coefficients-and-truncations]]: the domains $D(r)$ and $D_k$, the parameters $b=\rho/(8N)$, $r_N=\rho/(C_0MN)$, the binomial coefficients $\binom{s}{k}$, the difference operator $\Delta_h$, the truncated family $T_h^{s,N}$ and the truncated logarithm $L_N(h)$. Let $f,g$ be holomorphic on $D_0$. Here $D_j$ in a coefficient identity means the common inner domain $D(\rho/4)$, independent of the truncation order; $j=0,1$ coefficients are extracted using any truncation $N\ge\max\{2,j\}$. For $j\in\mathbb N$, $s\in\mathbb C$ and $Z\in D(\rho/4)$ define the **coefficient polynomial**

$$P_j(s)f:=\sum_{k=0}^{j}\binom{s}{k}\,\bigl[h^j\bigr]\bigl(\Delta_h^kf\bigr),$$

where $[h^j](\Delta_h^kf):=\frac{1}{j!}\partial_h^j\bigl(\Delta_h^kf\bigr)\big|_{h=0}$ is the $j$-th Taylor coefficient at $h=0$ of the function $h\mapsto(\Delta_h^kf)(Z)$, holomorphic for $|h|\le r_j$ by [[lem-cm-difference-operator-and-domain-loss-bound]]; thus $P_j(s)f$ is a polynomial of degree at most $j$ in $s$ with coefficients in the holomorphic functions on $D_j$.

Then:

1. **Integer case.** For all integers $Q\ge2$, $0\le m\le Q$ and every $|h|\le r_Q$, $T_h^{m,Q}f=f\circ\Psi_h^m$ on the domain $D_m$ allocated with order $Q$.
2. **Multiplicativity and bracket identity.** For every $j\in\mathbb N$ and every $s\in\mathbb C$, as identities of holomorphic functions on $D_j$,
 $$P_j(s)(fg)=\sum_{j_1+j_2=j}P_{j_1}(s)f\cdot P_{j_2}(s)g,\qquad P_j(s)\{f,g\}=\sum_{j_1+j_2=j}\bigl\{P_{j_1}(s)f,\;P_{j_2}(s)g\bigr\}.$$
3. **The logarithm is a derivation.** Put $D_jf:=P_j'(0)f\in\mathcal O(D_j)$ (the derivative in $s$ at $s=0$), so that $D_jf=[h^j]\bigl(L(h)f\bigr)$ for the formal logarithm $L(h):=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}\Delta_h^k$. Then $D_0=0$, each $D_j$ is a $\mathbb C$-linear local differential operator on holomorphic functions, and
 $$D_j(fg)=D_jf\cdot g+f\cdot D_jg,\qquad D_j\{f,g\}=\{D_jf,\,g\}+\{f,\,D_jg\}$$
as functions on $D_j$; equivalently the coefficient of $h^j$ in $L(h)(fg)$ and in $L(h)\{f,g\}$ obeys the product rule and the bracket derivation rule. Moreover $D_jf$ for $h$-degree $j\le N$ agrees with the $j$-th coefficient of the concrete holomorphic function $h\mapsto L_N(h)f$ restricted to $|h|\le r_N$ whenever $j\le N$.

Moreover $D_jf=\sum_i(D_jz_i)\partial_{z_i}f$ for $j\ge1$: each coefficient derivation is the coordinate vector field used in the later Hamiltonian construction.

Let $d\ge1$, let $(U,U_\rho,\tilde A,\tilde B,M,K,\delta,\Psi_h)$ be analytic splitting data, and use the notation of [[def-cm-modified-log-coefficients-and-truncations]] and [[lem-cm-difference-operator-and-domain-loss-bound]]: $b=\rho/(8N)$, $r_N=\rho/(C_0MN)$ with $C_0=\max\{16,128d^2\}$, the domains $D_k$, the difference operator $\Delta_h$, the truncated logarithm $L_N(h)$ and the coefficient fields $X_j$, $1\le j\le N$. Then for every integer $N\ge2$, every $|h|\le r_N$ and every coordinate index $i$:

1. $\lVert\Delta_h^kz_i\rVert_{D_k}\le2M|h|\,q^{k-1}$ for $1\le k\le N$, where $q=C_dM|h|/b\le1/4$.
2. The function $h\mapsto\frac{(L_N(h)z_i)(Z)}{h}$, initially defined for $0<|h|\le r_N$, extends holomorphically to the disc $|h|\le r_N$, and
 $$\left\lvert\frac{(L_N(h)z_i)(Z)}{h}\right\rvert\le\frac{2M}{1-q}\le\frac{8M}{3}\qquad(|h|\le r_N,\ Z\in D_N).$$
3. For $1\le j\le N$ and every $Z\in D_N$,
 $$\max_i\lvert(X_j)_i(Z)\rvert\le\frac{8M}{3}\,r_N^{-(j-1)},$$
 and the sharper estimate
 $$\max_i\lvert(X_j)_i(Z)\rvert\le\frac{8M}{3}\left(\frac{C_0Mj}{\rho}\right)^{j-1},$$
 obtained for $j\ge2$ by computing the $j$-th field with truncation order $j$, and for $j=1$ from $X_1=X_{\tilde A}+X_{\tilde B}$; the two bounds agree in the form $r_N^{-(j-1)}=(C_0MN/\rho)^{j-1}$.
The corresponding Euclidean field bounds are these component bounds multiplied by $\sqrt{2d}$.

4. The field $X_j$ is independent of the truncation order: if $N,N'\ge j$ then the $j$-th coefficient fields of $L_N$ and $L_{N'}$ agree on $D(\rho/4)$.

Let $d\ge1$, let $(U,U_\rho,\tilde A,\tilde B,M,K,\delta,\Psi_h)$ be analytic splitting data with $\tilde H:=\tilde A+\tilde B$, and let $X_j$, $j\ge1$, be the coefficient fields of [[def-cm-modified-log-coefficients-and-truncations]] (independent of the truncation order by [[lem-cm-truncated-log-coefficient-bounds]] clause 4), with the bound $\max_i\lvert(X_j)_i\rvert\le\beta_j:=\frac{8M}{3}\bigl(\frac{C_0Mj}{\rho}\bigr)^{j-1}$ of that lemma on the common retained domain $E:=D(\rho/4)$. In this item $D_j$ denotes $E$ for every $j\ge1$, including $j=1$, whose coefficient is extracted using any order $N\ge2$. Write $X_j=\sum_{k=1}^d u^{(j)}_k\partial_{z^k}+\sum_{k=1}^d v^{(j)}_k\partial_{w_k}$ in the coordinates $Z=(z,w)$ of [[def-cm-complex-phase-domains-and-holomorphic-maps]], and let $A_j:=\bigl(\partial_{Z_l}(X_j)_k\bigr)_{k,l}$ be its complex Jacobian. Then for every $j\ge1$:

1. $X_j$ is a holomorphic vector field on $D_j$: all $u^{(j)}_k,v^{(j)}_k$ are holomorphic on $D_j$ and real-valued on $D_j\cap\mathbb R^{2d}$.
2. $A_jJ+JA_j^{\mathsf T}=0$ on $D_j$; equivalently, the contraction one-form
 $$\alpha_j:=\iota_{X_j}\omega_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{k=1}^d u^{(j)}_k\,dw_k-\sum_{k=1}^d v^{(j)}_k\,dz^k$$
 is closed there.
3. There is a holomorphic $H_j:D_j\to\mathbb C$ with $dH_j=\alpha_j$, $H_j(0)=0$ and $H_j$ real-valued on $D_j\cap\mathbb R^{2d}$, and
 $$\lvert\nabla H_j\rvert\le\sqrt{2d}\,\beta_j,\qquad \lvert H_j(Z)\rvert\le\sqrt{2d}\,\beta_j\,\lvert Z\rvert\qquad(Z\in D_j).$$
4. $X_1=X_{\tilde H}=J\nabla\tilde H$; that is, for every holomorphic $f$ on the domain of $X_1$, $X_1f=d\!f(X_{\tilde H})$.

1. **Reversibility.** For every $h$ for which both sides are defined, $\Psi_{-h}=\Psi_h^{-1}$.
2. **Parity.** $X_j=0$ for every even $j\ge2$.
3. **Modified energy.** Consequently $H_2=0$, and the truncated modified Hamiltonian $H^{[N]}:=H+\sum_{j=2}^{N}h^{j-1}H_j$ equals $H+h^2H_3+\cdots+h^{N-1}H_N$ on $D_N$, so the first possible correction is of order $h^2$.

items.statement:
For the dimensionless oscillator $H(q,p)=(q^2+p^2)/2$, velocity Verlet is the matrix map $z\mapsto S_hz$, where

$$S_h=\begin{pmatrix}1-h^2/2&h\\-h(1-h^2/4)&1-h^2/2\end{pmatrix}.$$

For $0<h<2$, put $\alpha=1-h^2/4$ and $I_h(q,p)=(\alpha q^2+p^2)/2$. This positive quadratic form is exactly preserved. Every iterate satisfies

$$|H(z_n)-H(z_0)|\le\frac{h^2}{4\alpha}I_h(z_0).$$

The conclusion is an explicit exact-arithmetic all-step fact for this linear example. At $h=2$ positivity fails; at $h>2$ the map has a real eigenvalue of modulus greater than one.

items.statement: On the dimensionless real ball $U=B_4(0)\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, take $A(q,p)=1-\cos q$, $B(q,p)=p^2/2$, $\rho=1$ and $K=\overline B_2(0)$. The splitting is velocity Verlet. These data satisfy the analytic hypotheses with $M=5+\cosh(1)$. Therefore, for sufficiently small constant $h>0$, if the iterates lie in $K$ through $nh\le e^{c/(2h)}$, their original-energy deviation is $O(h^2)$. Compact retention is an additional hypothesis, which this example does not infer from the estimate.
